description: Draft an open call or a pro ask. An open call is a brief people answer with their own AI, checked against five requirements: a competition picks a winner; a hire pays every entry that passes, up to a number, and picks nobody; open to anyone, by application (you say yes to each), or by invitation (your list: addresses, @handles, single-use links). A software-review Ask (`kind: "review"`) is one specialised work type on Pro Asks: verified pros you invite try the scenarios and send reports; always a hire, by invitation only; Asky Pro Checker, the verifier, checks each report. Interviews in order: give what the person said, and the answer lists what is still missing, each with the question to ask them. Kept on disk between calls, so never re-send what was already taken. When nothing is missing it shows the whole call, what each leg holds (a pro ask's money in one sentence: what each pro receives, what is held per report, and the network's share (shown in the preview), the pro gets the rest) and the clock, for the person to approve. Spends nothing.

access.description: Who may enter an open call: anyone (listed), by application (listed; you say yes to each), or by invitation (not listed; only your list). A pro ask is by invitation only ("invite", its default).

brief.description: The task in plain words, up to eight short paragraphs. Start with what to make. Use one action per paragraph. Say what evidence to send and explain any spending limit. Avoid jargon and repeated explanations; keep payment conditions in the requirements too.

clear.description: Start this draft over. Refused once a leg is posted.

cover.description: A picture heading the call: an https address and words for it. null removes it.

diagram.description: A mermaid flowchart; its A --> B lines become numbered steps.

invite.description: Who to invite once the entries post: ixo1 addresses, @handles of people with a page, and "link" once per single-use link to mint. A pro ask may leave this out and invite after it posts (find_pro, then invite_to_call).

invite_note.description: A private note every person in invite reads with their invitation: access details such as a staging address or a test account. Only the invited people see it.

kind.description: review: a pro ask on Pro Asks, a review of an app or an agent. Verified pros you invite try the scenarios and hand in review reports; every report that passes the lines is paid the same (a hire); by invitation only; the five lines default to the review's own unless given. Asky Pro Checker, the verifier, checks each report for its own fee per check, held with the reward. Where Asky's report form is published, every report fills that form and Asky's own checks always apply; any lines you give beyond the review's defaults, and every extra report heading, are added as your own rules: the AI checks each, and a doubt goes to the person for the final OK.

lede.description: Two or three sentences under the title.

lines.description: The five requirements the jury reviews. For each, write the requirement in `text` and the condition that fails it in `fail`. Write `fail` as a clause completing "Fail this only if …", for example "it names no page". Include all five.

mode.description: competition: a pick and runners-up beside the paid entries. hire: every entry that passes is paid the same, up to a number, and nobody is picked.

money.description: In dollars. A competition: the pick's prize; runners-up, how many and each; what each entry that passes earns, and up to how many. A hire: only entry_each and entry_up_to.

network.description: Which deployment: `mainnet` is the real network (real money); `testnet` is the sandbox (play money, a dry run).

open_days.description: How many days entries stay open.

poster.description: How the poster wants to be named on the call.

report.description: A review: extra section headings every report must have, besides the standard summary, steps, findings, recommendations and limitations. Empty is fine. On Asky's report form each heading becomes a rule of yours: the report must cover it.

scenarios.description: A review: the scenarios to try, one line each; every report must cover each with a step.

slug.description: The call's name, for its page: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter. Omit for a random call-<hex> name; then use the name the answer gives.

start.description: A short message asking the entrant's AI to help prepare the work. The published page adds the ask's unique number and direct link. Require the person's approval before spending, publishing or submitting.

subject.description: A review: what is reviewed, the version to test, and where a specialist finds it (a public address). Private access goes in the invitation note, never here.

name: draft_call
title: Set up an open call or a pro ask
